Cadillac took a family wagon, stuffed a 6.2-liter supercharged V8 under the hood producing 556 horsepower and 551 lb-ft of torque, sent all of it to the rear wheels, and somehow convinced everyone this was a perfectly reasonable thing to sell. Sunroof.  Loaded with equipment.  And that unmistakable wide, aggressive CTS-V stance.  There's something hilarious about looking at the back of what appears to be a practical Cadillac wagon knowing there's a 556HP supercharged V8 hiding underneath the hood.  That's exactly why enthusiasts love these things.  It's a sleeper when you want it to be, a legitimately useful wagon when you need it to be, and a tire-smoking rear-wheel-drive V8 Cadillac whenever the mood strikes.  THREE CARS IN ONE.  We've had some seriously cool performance cars come through AutoPark Dallas, but the CTS-V Wagon will always have a special place in the enthusiast world.  They didn't make many.  They certainly don't build anything like it anymore.  And every year, finding a clean example gets a little harder.  Come see it in our indoor 40,000 Sq Ft showroom at AutoPark Dallas in Dallas, TX, surrounded by over 400 Performance, Luxury & Collector Cars. Supercharged V8. Rear-wheel drive. And enough room in the back for the groceries.  All wrapped up in a sinister black-on-black Cadillac wagon.  Guys...  HOW COOL IS THIS THING? description: A three-row SUV becomes much more useful when the second row is easy to access and the powertrain has enough strength to feel relaxed with passengers aboard, and this 2020 Ford Explorer XLT delivers both. Finished in Silver Metallic with a cloth interior, this four-wheel-drive Explorer uses Fords redesigned rear-wheel-drive-based platform, a 2.3-liter EcoBoost engine, and a spacious cabin to handle commuting, family travel, and everyday utility around Wesley Chapel and Tampa.  The turbocharged 2.3-liter EcoBoost four-cylinder is paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission and produces 300 horsepower, giving the Explorer confident response for highway merging, passing, and carrying a full load of passengers. Four-wheel drive adds traction for wet pavement, loose surfaces, and changing travel conditions, while selectable drive modes allow the driver to tailor vehicle behavior to different situations. The independent suspension helps the Explorer remain composed on longer drives and uneven roads.  XLT trim brings a useful upgrade in comfort without turning the cabin into something overly complicated. Unique cloth seating, a 10-way power drivers seat with lumbar support, a power front-passenger seat, and second-row captains chairs create a comfortable layout for daily family use. The captains chairs also make third-row access easier, while the third-row seat can be folded when cargo space becomes more important than passenger capacity.  Intelligent Access with push-button start makes getting in and underway simple, while the SecuriCode keypad provides another convenient way to access the vehicle without digging for a key. Dual second-row USB ports help passengers keep devices charged, and the leather-wrapped steering wheel with paddle shifters gives the driver easy access to common controls. Roof rails add flexibility for compatible cargo accessories when the interior is already full.  Ford Co-Pilot360 technology adds useful driver-assistance features for busy Tampa Bay traffic. Pre-Collision Assist with Automatic Emergency Braking, Blind Spot Information System with Cross-Traffic Alert, Lane-Keeping System, Auto High-Beam Headlamps, and a rearview camera help support awareness without changing the Explorers natural driving feel. Stability control, traction control, and four-wheel antilock disc brakes add another layer of support in changing conditions.  Cargo flexibility is a major reason to choose an Explorer. With all three rows in use there is still room for everyday bags and groceries, while folding the third row opens a much larger area for luggage, sports gear, home-improvement supplies, or travel equipment. Fold more of the rear seating and the Explorer can handle bulkier items that would be difficult to fit in a sedan or smaller crossover.  This Explorer is Ford Blue Certified, adding a 139-point inspection, a 90-day/4,000-mile Comprehensive Limited Warranty, 24/7 Roadside Assistance, and applicable FordPass Rewards Points.  For a buyer who needs three rows, strong turbocharged power, four-wheel-drive confidence, and enough cargo flexibility for real family life, this Explorer XLT remains a very practical choice.
